event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: AMGN’s 2023 Form 10-K embeds a concentrated cluster of disclosures that tie the continuing COVID-19 pandemic to multiple, material risk vectors across virtually every link of the company’s value-chain.  Management acknowledges that the pandemic has already produced concrete, negative outcomes—ranging from lower product demand and reduced patient access to clinical-trial disruption and supply-chain shortages—and expressly warns that these pressures are expected to persist.  The language is current-tense (“are adversely affecting”) and forward-looking (“expected to continue”), with repeated use of severity qualifiers such as “material adverse effect” and “significantly,” leaving little doubt that the company views the threat as both ongoing and potentially escalating.  Because the filing date (Feb 2023) sits less than three years after the WHO-declared start of the pandemic (Mar 2020), the Time Decay Principle permits elevated severity scores.  The statements are highly specific—naming clinical trials, manufacturing plants, labour availability, supply-chain logistics, product demand and receivables—yet they are not mitigated by detailed counter-measures or quantified financial buffers.  Taken together, the evidence supports high, but not maximum, snippet scores in the 5-9 range.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic, and the public and governmental effort to mitigate against the spread of the disease, have had, and are expected to continue to have, an adverse effect, and may have a material adverse effect, on our clinical trials, operations, manufacturing, supply chains, distribution systems, product development, product sales, business and results of operations.

components.reason: States impacts have already occurred ("have had") – realised harm.
Projects continued and potentially ‘material’ adverse effects – forward-looking severity.
Enumerates a broad list of core functions affected (clinical trials, manufacturing, supply chain, sales).
Uses strong adverse language: "material adverse effect."

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly links COVID-19 to past and future material harm across multiple business pillars, justifying a high severity score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and the resulting measures implemented in response to the pandemic are adversely affecting, and are expected to continue to adversely affect, our business (including our R&D, clinical trials, operations, manufacturing, supply chains, distribution systems, product development and sales activities), the business activities of our suppliers, customers, third-party payers and our patients.

components.reason: Confirms current adverse impacts and continuation thereof.
Highlights ripple effects on external stakeholders (suppliers, customers, payers, patients) increasing systemic risk.
Specific operational domains listed, demonstrating breadth.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows ongoing, wide-ranging operational and ecosystem impacts, earning a strong score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Due to the pandemic and these measures and their effects, we have experienced, and expect to continue to experience, unpredictable reductions in demand for certain of our products, exacerbated by COVID-19 surges resulting in repeated shutdowns and/or disruptions in certain geographies.

components.reason: Identifies realised revenue pressure through demand reductions.
Emphasises unpredictability and continuation of the effect.
Links effect to geographic shutdowns, showing external dependency.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specifies actual demand hits and forecasts ongoing volatility; substantial but narrower than prior snippets, thus a 6.

evidence_list.snippet: These measures and challenges will likely continue to varying degrees and have significantly reduced patient access to, and administration of, certain of our drugs.

components.reason: Confirms significant reduction in patient access—direct revenue and health impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Notes concrete reduction in patient throughput with expectation of persistence; moderate-high impact merits score 5.

evidence_list.snippet: As the pandemic continues, and if conditions worsen or if the duration of the pandemic extends significantly, we expect to experience additional adverse effects on our development, operational and commercial activities, customer purchases and our collections of accounts receivable.

components.reason: Flags potential for broader future harm across development, operations, sales and cash collection.
Conditional language highlights escalation risk if pandemic worsens or persists.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking statement covering multiple financial/operational fronts; risk is contingent but wide, yielding a 5.

evidence_list.snippet: These measures could significantly affect our ability to support our operations and customers and the ability of our employees to get to their workplaces to discover, study, develop and produce our product candidates and products, disrupt the movement of our products through the supply chain, and further prevent or discourage patients from participating in our clinical trials, seeking healthcare services and the administration of certain of our products.

components.reason: Details operational disruptions: workforce, supply chain, clinical trials.
Uses strong modifier “significantly affect,” indicating severity.
Highlights patient participation barrier—demand side risk.
Covers both internal operations and external logistics, demonstrating systemic exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive yet conditional description of operational chokepoints; aggregate weight leads to score 5.
